themes: Allah is the most just judge
summary_for_children: At-Tin means The Fig. It swears by the fig, the olive, Mount Sinai and the safe city, and says Allah created people in the best form, and those who believe and do good have an endless reward.
world_title: Fig, Olive and the Secure City
environment_concept: The path runs between a fig orchard and an olive grove (95:1). Far off stands a tall mountain for Mount Sinai (95:2) and a small walled city in a valley for the secure city (95:3). Both are simple stand-ins seen from far away, not their real shapes. No person is shown.
architecture_and_scenery: Fig trees with broad leaves and purple fruit, silver-green olive trees, a far mountain, a far walled city.

depiction_rules: No prophet, person or representation of Allah is shown. Unseen realities are never pictured. Interactive activities are labelled as adaptations.

unique_world.visual_theme: A terraced hillside of olive and fig trees at the end of the harvest with an old stone olive press on the top terrace

primary_mechanic.text: Press the olive harvest the traditional way: turn the millstone to crush the olives, spread the paste on woven mats, tighten the press a little at a time (tightening again before the oil has run is refused), then let the jar settle and skim the oil that floats on the watery juice (skimming early or pouring from the bottom is refused). Oil floats on water: real.

secondary_activities: the most just of judges (95:7-8, read)
unique_world.narrative_structure: A reading among the fig trees, the olive press, then a reading on the top terrace
environment_behaviour: the basin fills with paste, the mats flatten, and the jar turns golden
unique_world.learning_objective: Know that man was created in the best of form (95:4)

story_library.source: Owner's 'Quran Adventure — Children's Story Library' (2026-11-04), first-draft narration for ages about 7-12
story_library.title: The Fig and the Olive
story_library.children_narration: Surah At-Tin begins with oaths by the fig and olive, Mount Sinai, and the secure city. It reminds us that human beings were created with dignity and are responsible for their faith and actions.

world_idea.title: The Orchard of Dignity
world_idea.description: Explore fig and olive trees, discover their natural characteristics, and visit symbolic learning spaces connected to the surah's themes.
